sections.heading: C — Basic driving
sections.markdown:
## C — Basic driving (Section 8)

Coverage basis: pedagogic_emphasis only; no official exam weights were supplied, so depth follows test relevance [A01].

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
A driver begins with the selector in park or the clutch engaged and the brake held, then checks lamps and gauges before moving [A01].
Why it matters: prevents unintended motion at startup.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
When backing, the driver looks through the rear window with one arm over the passenger seat, steers toward the intended rear path, and never backs on a freeway or interstate [A01].
Why it matters: mirrors leave a blind zone directly behind.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
A lane change requires mirror checks, a signal held for at least two seconds, an over-shoulder blind-spot check, and a safe merge before cancelling [A01].
Why it matters: sequencing prevents side collisions.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A02
A driver stays inside marked lanes, finishes a turn in the lane corresponding to the entry lane, and avoids lane changes inside intersections [A02].
Why it matters: lane discipline is directly scored.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A02
A merging driver yields to traffic already in the continuing lane and never drives across or inside the solid-white gore area [A02].
Why it matters: gore separation protects diverge points.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A02
At a congested merge point drivers use the zipper method by filling both lanes to the merge point and then alternating entry into the single lane [A02].
Why it matters: fixes early-merge congestion errors.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A02
At a stop sign or signal the driver stops before the stop line, crosswalk, sidewalk, or intersection, and behind another vehicle leaves room to see its rear wheels [A02].
Why it matters: stop position is a common fail point.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A03
For downhill parking the driver signals right, pulls parallel to the curb, turns the front wheels toward the curb so a tire contacts it, then sets park and the parking brake [A03].
Why it matters: curb contact blocks downhill roll.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A04
For uphill parking with a curb the driver turns the front wheels away from the curb with tire contact, and without a curb turns them to the right, then sets park and the brake [A04].
Why it matters: opposite of downhill; highly confusable.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A04
A parked vehicle beside a curb sits no more than 12 inches from the curb, with the motor stopped, brake set, and doors locked [A04].
Why it matters: exact distance is testable.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A05
A passing driver enters the left lane after checks and signal, returns no less than 200 feet from oncoming traffic, and never leaves the roadway to pass on the right [A05].
Why it matters: combines distance and roadway limits.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A05
Passing is prohibited with oncoming traffic, blocked view on a curve or hill, at intersections and stopped crosswalks, before rail crossings and bridges, in no-passing zones, and beside a deployed snowplow blade or echelon formation [A05].
Why it matters: list-style exam trap.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A06
Signals by lamp or hand and arm are required for two seconds before turning, for two seconds before any lane change, and whenever pulling to or from a curb [A06].
Why it matters: timing rule repeats across maneuvers.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A06
The driver keeps both hands on the outside of the wheel, grips with fingers rather than palms, and turns the wheel toward the intended travel direction in forward or reverse [A06].
Why it matters: steering posture underlies every maneuver.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A06
At a rail crossing controlled by signals, gates, a watchman, or a stop sign the driver stops more than 15 feet but not more than 50 feet from the nearest rail and waits for a raised gate [A06].
Why it matters: exact stopping window is testable.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A07
Traffic both directions stops for flashing red school-bus lights on a two-lane road and on a four-lane road without a median, while only the lanes behind the bus stop on a median-divided highway with four or more lanes and on a highway with five or more lanes plus a shared center turn lane [A07].
Why it matters: roadway-type distinction is the trap.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A09
A driver never makes a U-turn where visibility is blocked within 500 feet in both directions, where a device prohibits it, on rail tracks or crossings, or on a freeway [A09].
Why it matters: combines distance and location bans.
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0048]

High-yield ranked: stopping and school-bus rules first, then lane-change and passing limits, then parking placement, then merge and U-turn limits.
Misconceptions: mirrors alone suffice for backing; gore paint may be crossed; early merge is always correct; only same-direction traffic stops for buses.
Mnemonics: downhill wheels to curb like rolling to curb; uphill wheels away to catch the curb; zipper merge like teeth alternating.
Glossary: gore area is the solid-white bordered zone between continuing and entering or exiting lanes; head check is an over-shoulder blind-spot look; zipper method is alternating entry at a congested merge.
Dynamic-fact isolation: no time or location-variable facts in these pages; city U-turn ordinances noted as locally variable and left to the cited handbook rule.
